Indemnification of Directors and Officers. Under the Texas Business Organizations Code (the “TBOC”), the charter of a corporation may provide that a director or officer of the corporation is not liable, or is liable only to the extent provided by the charter, to the corporation or its shareholders for monetary damages for an act or omission by the person in the person’s capacity as a director or officer. The TBOC does not authorize elimination or limitation of liability to the extent the director or officer is found liable under applicable law for: • any breach of the director’s or officer’s duty of loyalty to the corporation or its shareholders; • any act or omission not in good faith that constitutes a breach of duty of the director or officer to the corporation or that involves intentional misconduct or a knowing violation of law; • any transaction from which the director or officer receives an improper benefit, whether or not the benefit resulted from an action taken within the scope of the director’s duties; or • an act or omission for which the liability of the director or officer is expressly provided by an applicable statute. Our charter will provide that our directors and officers are not liable to the Company or its shareholders for monetary damages for an act or omission by the director or officer in his or her capacity as a director or officer or for a breach of any duty as a director or officer to the fullest extent permitted by the TBOC, as it exists or as amended from time to time. The TBOC provides that a corporation must indemnify a director or former director against reasonable expenses actually incurred by the person in connection with a proceeding in which the person is a respondent because the person is or was a director, or is or was serving as a representative of another enterprise or organization or an employee benefit plan while serving as a director, if the director or former director is wholly successful, on the merits or otherwise, in the defense of the proceeding. If a court determines that a director, former director or representative is entitled to indemnification, the court will order indemnification by the corporation and award the person expenses incurred in securing the indemnification. The TBOC also permits corporations to indemnify present or former directors where indemnification is not mandated by the TBOC; however, such permissive indemnification is subject to certain limitations and the director satisfying specified standards of conduct. The TBOC also provides that officers must be indemnified to the same extent as directors are required to be indemnified under the TBOC and that a court may also order indemnification under various circumstances. In addition, the TBOC permits indemnification in certain circumstances in which we would not otherwise have the power to do so under the II-2 Table of Contents provisions of the TBOC or our charter or bylaws if that indemnification is approved by the shareholders of the Company. Our bylaws will also provide that, to the fullest extent permitted by the TBOC, the Company must indemnify any person who was or is, or is threatened to be made, a party to any threatened, pending or completed action, suit or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, arbitrative, legislative or investigative, including an appeal thereof, by reason of the fact that the person is or was a director or an officer (who is appointed by our board or specifically designated as such by our chief executive officer, president or chief financial officer) of the Company, or while a director or officer of the Company is or was serving at the request of the Company as a director, officer, partner, venturer, trustee, employee, administrator or agent of another entity, trust or enterprise, against expenses (including attorneys’ fees), judgments, penalties, fines and amounts paid in settlement actually and reasonably incurred by the person in connection with the action, suit or proceeding if the person satisfied a specified standard of conduct. Our bylaws will also provide that expenses (including attorneys’ fees) actually and reasonably incurred by such director or officer in defending any proceeding will be paid by the Company in advance of the final disposition of the proceeding upon written request from that person subject to the person satisfying certain conditions. To the extent that indemnification for liabilities arising under the Securities Act may be permitted to our directors, officers and controlling persons, we have been advised that, in the opinion of the SEC, this indemnification is against public policy as expressed in the Securities Act and is, therefore, unenforceable. The TBOC and our bylaws permit the Company to purchase insurance on behalf of existing or former officers, employees, directors or agents against any liability asserted against and incurred by that person in such capacity, or arising out of that person’s status in such capacity, whether or not the Company would have the power to indemnify that person under the TBOC. Pursuant to this authority, we expect to obtain such insurance for the officers, employees, directors and agents of the Company and its subsidiaries. We will also enter into written indemnification agreements with each of our officers and directors that provide, in general, that we will indemnify them against loss and liability arising from, and will pay or reimburse their actual and reasonable expenses incurred in advance of the final disposition of any legal proceeding involving their service to us or on our behalf. As permitted by the TBOC, because these agreements are expected to be approved by our shareholders, the agreements may require indemnification or payment of expenses in favor of the indemnitee in certain circumstances in which we would not otherwise have the power to do so under the provisions of the TBOC or our charter or bylaws. Pursuant to a written undertaking provided by any director or officer who requests the Company to reimburse or pay that person’s expenses in advance of the final disposition of the proceeding, the director or officer will be required to repay the advanced expenses to the Company if it is found that such director or officer is not entitled to indemnification under applicable law and our bylaws. The proposed form of Underwriting Agreement filed as Exhibit 1.1 to this Registration Statement will provide for indemnification of our directors and officers by the underwriters against certain liabilities in connection with this offering. 比亚迪 vs 特斯拉 · 基金经理视角 基金经理视角 · 开场 如果你是基金经理， 你根本不会"这样"比这两家 普通人把财务指标一列，比谁毛利率高、谁 ROE 高。 但一个真正的 PM，第一反应是—— 拒绝这种比较 。 🎯 因为他知道：比亚迪和特斯拉，根本不是同一类资产，不能塞进同一个估值框架里比。 那他会怎么比？先把"它们是什么"说清楚 ↓ 大前提 · 它们是两种资产 一个卖"确定的现金流"， 一个卖"不确定的期权" 比亚迪 一台现在就赚钱的 制造业效率机器 Alpha 来源：垂直整合 · 规模 · 成本曲线下移 · 全球扩张 估值锚：制造业 / 周期成长 久期：短 → 对利率不敏感，对中国需求·价格战·关税敏感 特斯拉 一个押注未来的 期权 / 叙事资产 市值不在卖车：FSD · Optimus · Robotaxi · AI · 储能 估值锚：科技成长 / 远期期权 久期：超长 → 对利率·风险偏好·叙事极度敏感 🔍 一句话定调 PE 372 倍说明：市场 根本没在给特斯拉的汽车业务定价 ，而是在给"它可能成为一个 AI + 机器人平台"定价。所以你不是在比两家车企——你是在比 一个确定的现金流，和一个不确定的远期期权 。 定下基调，再看比较里的"坑" ↓ 对比的陷阱 先记住：抠绝对数字没意义， 看趋势和结构才对 📐 会计准则 CAS vs GAAP 📦 合并范围 含手机代工 vs 含能源 📈 发展阶段 扩张期 vs 稳定期 🏛️ 估值体系 A/H 股 vs 纳斯达克 💱 货币 人民币 vs 美元 🧩 赚钱逻辑 硬件 vs 软件/AI ⚠️ PE 差 12 倍，不是公司差 12 倍；同一笔业务两套准则能算出不同利润。带着这些坑，往下看。 坑记住了 → 先看表面，再下刀 ↓ BYD 002594 vs TSLA · 2025年报 表面上，两家 净利率几乎一模一样 📊 净利率 4.06% vs 4.00% ｜ 毛利率 17.75% vs 18.03% 看着像双胞胎——但底下的生意，天差地别 比亚迪 2025 8,040亿 营收 · 460万辆 · 净利≈326亿 特斯拉 2025 6,458亿 营收(折RMB) · 164万辆 · 净利≈260亿 🔍 注意：一样的是"净利率"，不是"净利润" 两家 净利率 几乎相同（4.06% vs 4.00%），但因营收规模不同， 净利润绝对值差约 25% （约 326 亿 vs 260 亿）。真正值得追问的是——同样的薄利润率，是用 完全不同的生意 做出来的。下面六刀，刀刀切这个"不同"。 第一刀：这两个"差不多"的毛利率，都被化了妆 ↓ 第一刀 · 盈利质量 剥掉会计噪音： 毛利率被"化妆"过 比亚迪 合并范围：汽车 + 手机 + 电池 汽车毛利率 20.49% 手机代工毛利率 ≈5.99% → 合并毛利率被拉低 17.75% 单车均价 / 单车毛利 14.1万 / 2.89万 特斯拉 合并范围：汽车 + 能源 + 服务 汽车毛利率(GAAP) 17.8% 剔除零成本碳积分后 ≈15.3% 能源毛利率(抬高合并) 29.8% 单车均价 / 单车毛利 28.9万 / 5.15万 🔍 PM 只看"还原后的真实差距" 合并口径 17.75% vs 18.03%，"差不多"是假象。还原到 汽车主业 ：比亚迪 20.49% vs 特斯拉 17.8%；再剔掉特斯拉那笔近零成本的碳积分（约 $19.9 亿），特斯拉只剩 ≈15.3% ——真实差距从 2.7 个点拉大到 5.1 个点 。 而且方向相反： 比亚迪毛利在价格战中守住，特斯拉从 2022 年近 30% 一路滑到 15.3%。斜率，比快照更致命。 第二刀：别看历史 ROE，看"新投的每一块钱回报" ↓ 第二刀 · 增量回报 不看历史 ROE， 看"新砸下去的钱"赚不赚 比亚迪 2025 资本开支 1,568亿 泰国/巴西/匈牙利/印尼建厂+滚装船 经营现金流覆盖 Capex 37.7% 591亿 ÷ 1,568亿 特斯拉 2025 资本开支 581亿 工厂高峰已过，钱转投 AI/FSD 🔍 PM 真正担心的两个问题 对比亚迪： 一年砸 1568 亿建厂，经营现金流只能覆盖 38%，差额靠融资补。要问的不是"ROE 多高"，而是—— 这些新厂的回报率是多少？会不会扩张过头变产能过剩？ 这是它最大的变量。 对特斯拉： Capex 降下来了，但钱转投 FSD / Optimus / AI 算力（研发同比 +41%）—— 这些投入的回报极不确定，是在为"期权"续费。 历史 ROE 好看没用，决定未来的是 下一块钱投出去赚不赚 。 第三刀：负债率差 30 个点，到底是不是风险？ ↓ 第三刀 · 资产负债表压力测试 负债率 70.75% vs 39.87% 但 ROE 的高，几乎全靠杠杆 项目 比亚迪 特斯拉 PM 解读 资产负债率 70.75% 39.87% 差 30.9 个点，但大头不是"欠银行" 应付账款 2,092亿 911亿 占款=无息融资，是议价能力 有息负债 1,245亿 570亿 仅占负债差距 1/4，才是真债务 现金 / 短期投资 754亿 3,001亿 特斯拉净现金，财务"干净" ROE 12.61% 4.62% 4.06%×0.91× 3.42 vs 4.00%×0.69× 1.67 🔍 ROE 高 2.7 倍 ≠ 经营效率高 2.7 倍 杜邦拆开：净利率势均力敌，周转率比亚迪略胜， 差距几乎全在权益乘数（3.42 vs 1.67） ——比亚迪用应付账款 + 合同负债（约 2,607 亿零成本经营负债）撬动资产。若把杠杆降到特斯拉水平，ROE 约降到 6.2%。 压力测试结论： 论估值便宜、盈利实在，PM 偏比亚迪；论熊市/流动性收紧下的抗冲击力，特斯拉净现金的资产负债表更稳。 买谁，取决于你押的是什么环境。 第四刀：两家都有护城河，但"性质"完全不同 ↓ 第四刀 · 护城河的性质 成本护城河 vs 软件护城河 一个会被追赶，一个可能不兑现 比亚迪 · 成本护城河 来源 垂直整合 / 规模 强度 现实、可兑现 软肋 可被中国同行追赶 信号 价格战=护城河正被侵蚀 特斯拉 · 软件护城河 来源 FSD / 数据 / 网络效应 强度 更高、更持久 软肋 可能永远不兑现 信号 FSD 落地进度=兑现与否 🏰 你信"看得见、但会被追上"的成本优势，还是信"看不见、但一旦成真就赢家通吃"的软件网络？——你信哪种护城河，决定你买哪个。 马斯克 key-man 叙事波动 估值均值回归 本质是一张"长久期科技期权"，对利率上行和叙事降温极度敏感，押的是一个人和一个未来。 🔍 PM 的真实操作 他不会孤立地"选一个好的"，而是问： 我的组合现在缺哪种暴露？ 两者风险来源几乎不重叠——可能两个都配来对冲，也可能因为已经超配中国/科技而都不碰。 "买谁"是组合问题，不是公司问题。 第六刀：买之前，先把"我会怎么亏钱"写下来 ↓ 第六刀 · 比亚迪 vs 特斯拉 · 哪些能比，哪些不能比（终版） 拆解上市公司 · 有二财经 如果我是比亚迪，我一定会想： 凭什么特斯拉能 372 倍 PE， 我才 30 倍 ？ 这个差距合理吗？还是说市场瞎了？ 🔥 我一年卖的车是特斯拉的近 3 倍，赚的钱也不比特斯少——但它的市值是我的 12 倍。我表示不服，很多买了比亚迪的人也不服，心里想着这么好的公司肯定是被低估了，想着以后肯定能到特斯拉那个级别。 为了搞清楚这些疑问，我准备把比亚迪和特斯拉这两个企业做个对比，简称" 比特比 "。哈哈哈。 动手之前 · 先认清一件事 把数字一列就比高低？ 这 4 条 局限性 先看清楚 谁要是把数字简单一列就比高低，一定会比错——先看清这 4 条 🔬 ① 披露颗粒度不同（最要命） 美股 10-K 把分部收入+成本都单列，能算到纯业务；A股年报常只到大类。同一个"汽车毛利率"，特斯拉能拆到 15.3%，比亚迪只到 20.48% 大类——能比到多深，先天就不一样。 🧩 ② 业务也有很多不同 比亚迪： 乘用车、商用车、电池、储能、手机代工、云轨、半导体、金融、矿产……（全在报表里） 特斯拉： 汽车、碳积分、能源、超充/保险、FSD软件、AI/机器人 两家"集团毛利率"里裹的业务完全不同——直接比，是拿苹果比橘子。 📈 ③ 发展阶段不同 比亚迪还在疯狂建厂（扩张期，自由现金流为负），特斯拉工厂高峰已过（成熟期，自由现金流为正）。同一个指标，含义完全不同。 🏛️ ④ 市场与估值体系不同 A+H 股 vs 纳斯达克：投资者结构、定价逻辑两套——一个按制造业定价（PE 30），一个按未来期权定价（PE 372）。PE 差 12 倍，不是公司差 12 倍。 注：会计准则 CAS vs GAAP 现在差异不大、能对清楚（最相关的就一个研发资本化口径），口径调一下即可；货币按汇率统一折算，不单列。 局限都清楚了 —— 直接来，全局对比 ↓ 全局对比 两家到底是不是一类？ 先把全貌摆出来 一趟讲完——从业务、家底、利润、现金流全摆出来，最后回到估值 ① 估值 —— 先看市场给的最终答案 📈 市值 比亚迪 ~0.8万亿 特斯拉 ~10万亿 PE 30 vs 372，PB 3.6 vs 18.15—— 12 倍。凭什么？ 🔍 市场给了一个悬殊的答案。那两家的生意本身差在哪？↓ ② 业务 —— PE差12倍，先看两家到底怎么做生意的 🚗 销量（2025全年） 比亚迪 460万 特斯拉 164万 差 2.8 倍——但数量≠质量 ↓ 🚙 单车均价 比亚迪 ≈11.9万 特斯拉 ≈28.9万 单价差 2.4 倍—— 数量差2.8倍、单价差2.4倍，两条路从根上就不同。 那收入上谁大？↓ ——但手机代工净利率只有1.8%，拉低了整体。剔除后：汽车分部净利率 比亚迪4.60% vs 特斯拉4.00%，比亚迪更高。 那PE差12倍不是差在利润率。看人效 ↓ 🎯 PM视角：汽车分部净利率比亚迪4.60%高于特斯拉4.00%——手机代工（净利率1.8%）拉低了集团到4.06%。比亚迪用70万人（纯汽车）、靠硬件；特斯拉用14万人、卖高价车+软件。 人均产出差4倍 ——这就是制造业和科技公司的本质区别。 👷 员工人数 比亚迪 ~70万 特斯拉 ~14万 5 倍差距 → 人均产出车 ≈6.6辆 vs ≈11.7辆（1.8倍）、人均营收 ≈115万 vs ≈461万（4倍）、人均净利 ≈4.7万 vs ≈18.4万（3.9倍）。制造业堆人、科技靠自动化 🎯 PM视角：70万人（纯汽车业务，已扣除手机代工约17万人）堆出的规模——市场看到的是"制造业的效率机器"，给的是制造业的估值。14万人撑起的AI叙事——市场看到的是"可能变成AI平台的期权"。 业务数据本身就在告诉市场：给比亚迪30倍、给特斯拉372倍，不是没道理。 ③ 资产负债表 —— 家底扛不扛得住 🏗️ 总资产 比亚迪 8,837亿 特斯拉 9,386亿 家底差不多——但结构不同：特斯拉现金多，比亚迪厂房设备多。资产结构后面专拆。那负债呢？↓ ⚖️ 资产负债率 比亚迪 70.75% 特斯拉 39.87% 差 30 个点——但大头是应付账款（占供应商无息的钱、议价能力），不是欠银行。总资产差不太多，负债率差这么多，净资产呢？↓ 📦 净资产 比亚迪 2,586亿 特斯拉 5,594亿 差 2 倍——特斯拉利润滚存+融资多年，比亚迪还在扩张。 📊 ROE（净资产收益率） 比亚迪 12.61% 特斯拉 4.62% 比亚迪ROE是特斯拉的2.7倍——但拆开看， 比亚迪ROE的高几乎全靠杠杆（权益乘数3.42 vs 1.67），不是经营效率 。若把杠杆降到特斯拉水平，ROE约降到6.2%。 🎯 若把杠杆降到特斯拉水平，ROE约降到6.2%。高负债≠高风险，但不等于高本事。 ④ 现金流 —— 钱去哪了 💵 货币资金 比亚迪 754亿 特斯拉 3,001亿 特斯拉现金是比亚迪 4 倍——赚差不多，但赚来的钱留住没有，看完账上看流水 ↓ 💧 经营现金流 比亚迪 591亿 特斯拉 1,004亿 含金量（÷净利润）1.81倍 vs 3.89倍——每赚1块，特斯拉真进账3.89块。经营流入这么多——钱砸哪了？↓ 🔧 资本支出 Capex（扩产/建厂） 比亚迪 1,568亿 特斯拉 581亿 比亚迪是特斯拉的 2.7 倍—— 全球建厂、扩产能，砸下去的都是真金白银 。经营流入这么多——钱砸哪了？↓ 🔬 研发投入（2025） 比亚迪 634亿 特斯拉 437亿 绝对值比亚迪多砸200亿——但投向/记账口径完全不同 ↓ 比亚迪 · 砸"现在"（硬件） · 刀片电池 / 动力电池 · DM 混动系统 · IGBT / SiC 车规芯片 → 投下去，受益的是几百款在产车型 特斯拉 · 砸"未来"（软件/AI） · FSD 全自动驾驶 / Robotaxi · Optimus 人形机器人 · Dojo 超算 / xAI → 大部分 还没营收 ，纯在研发费里烧 扩产砸完了、研发也砸完了——减掉这些，自由现金流还剩多少？↓ 💰 自由现金流（经营 − Capex） 比亚迪 −977亿 特斯拉 +424亿 一个烧钱扩张（Capex 1,568亿）、一个赚钱有余（581亿）—— 这是整个对比里最本质的差异。 🎯 PM视角：比亚迪一年砸 1,568亿建厂，经营现金流只能覆盖 38%，差额靠融资补—— 要问的不是"ROE多高"，而是"新砸下去的这些厂，回报率是多少？会不会扩张过头变产能过剩？" 特斯拉 Capex 降到 581亿，钱转投 FSD/Optimus—— 这些投入极不确定，是在为"期权"续费。 一个在赌规模、一个在赌未来，两个都押了巨大的注——只是赌的东西不同。 🔑 四块全摆出来，画像很清楚： 比亚迪 = 人海+重资产+高杠杆+烧钱扩张的"制造巨人"；特斯拉 = 人少+高自动化+现金充裕的"科技公司"。 一个在烧钱扩张、一个在赚钱等待。 ⑤ 回到估值 —— PE 30 vs 372，差12倍 📈 市盈率 PE 比亚迪 30 特斯拉 372 市场给比亚迪定价—— 定的就是财报上的东西 · 460万辆销量 · 70万人（纯汽车）堆起来的规模 · 8,040亿营收、4%净利率 · 海外建厂、全球扩张 → 定价锚：制造业 PE 30 PB 3.6 市场给特斯拉定价—— 定的不是160万辆，是这些 · FSD 全自动驾驶 · Optimus 人形机器人 · Robotaxi 出行网络 · Dojo 超算 / xAI → 这些，财报里全没收入 PE 372 PB 18.15 💡 差距在这：不是公司差12倍，是市场在买两种东西 比亚迪的估值锚： 460万辆车、70万人（纯汽车）堆出的规模、8040亿营收、4%净利率、-977亿自由现金流—— 买的是确定的制造能力和扩张预期。 特斯拉的估值锚： FSD、机器人、AI、Robotaxi—— 买的是一个不确定的远期期权。 所以你不是在比两家车企——你是在比 一个确定的现金流，和一个不确定的未来 。 PM 的元问题 —— 也是你的 "市场在每家身上，定价了 什么预期 ？ 我和市场的 分歧 在哪？" 投资赚的从来不是"好公司"的钱，是" 市场把预期定错了 "的钱。 比亚迪被当成"普通制造业"，是不是低估了它的全球化？ 特斯拉372倍里隐含的FSD成功概率，是高于还是低于真实概率？ 盈利能力 · 毛利率 先看特斯拉： "汽车毛利率"能一层层剥出来 特斯拉这个"汽车毛利率"到底怎么来的—— 从全公司往下，一层层剥 ： 全公司（车+服务+能源） 18.0% ↓ 剥掉「能源」（储能/光伏，自身毛利 29.8% 偏高 → 数字往下走） 汽车 + 服务 16.2% ↓ 剥掉「服务」（超充/二手/配件，自身毛利 7.4% 偏低 → 数字往上走） 纯汽车 · 含碳积分 ← 本片用这个 17.8% ↓ 剥掉「碳积分」（$1,993M，近零成本 → 数字往下走） 纯车 · 造车本身 15.3% 可即便都取"纯车口径"，两家篮子里 装的东西还是不一样 ： 这个毛利率里装了什么 比亚迪 20.48% 特斯拉 17.8% 整车销售 ✓ ✓ 汽车租赁 ✓ ✓ 碳积分 几乎没有 ✓ 含 动力电池外售 ✓ 含 ✗ 储能 / 光伏 ✓ 含 ✗ 单列在能源 云轨 / 半导体 ✓ 含 ✗ 🧺 比亚迪的"篮子"里多塞了电池、储能、云轨；特斯拉这 17.8% 是干干净净的车。装的东西不一样，20.48% 和 17.8% 根本不在一条起跑线上——谁也别拿它定"造车谁更赚"。 那比亚迪呢？它能不能也这么拆？↓ 盈利 · 比亚迪毛利 再看比亚迪： 纯造车毛利，年报根本没披露 特斯拉能从全公司 18% 一路剥到纯车 15.3%；轮到比亚迪—— 汽车及相关产品（大类） 20.48% ↓ 想再往下拆"纯整车毛利"？比亚迪没披露乘用车成本——剥不动 ✋ 纯整车毛利率 ？ 比亚迪披露的毛利率， 最细只到两个大类 ，再往下就没有了： 比亚迪的毛利率，最细到这一层 毛利率 能再往下拆吗 汽车及相关产品 含整车+电池外售+储能+云轨+半导体 20.48% ✗ 没单列成本 手机部件、组装 ≈ 比亚迪电子 00285.HK 6.29% ✓ 它本就独立上市 🔒 这就是两家最大的不对称：特斯拉把汽车分部的成本单列了， 纯车毛利能算到 15.3% ；比亚迪把整车、电池、储能全打包， 纯造车到底赚多少，年报根本没给数 。 🔍 那"纯造车毛利"就真没法知道了吗？ 年报口径只到大类、没单列纯整车成本，所以 官方数据算不出 。但这不等于无解—— 券商研报、专门"拆车"测算 BOM（物料成本）的第三方机构，是能把单车成本估出来的 。只是这些都是 外部估算、非官方、口径各异、有误差 。 记住：报表没披露 ≠ 无法知道，只是得换个地方找、并且接受它是"估的"。 盈利说完了 → 再深挖 ROE，最容易被表面数字骗 ↓ 深挖 · ROE 与杠杆 比亚迪 ROE 是特斯拉的 2.7 倍 ——是它更会赚钱吗？ 比亚迪 ROE 12.61% 净资产收益率 特斯拉 ROE 4.62% 净资产收益率 🤔 差 2.7 倍，看起来比亚迪碾压。把它拆开，结论可能跟你想的相反。 用杜邦公式，把 ROE 拆成三块 ↓ 杜邦拆解 ROE = 净利率 × 周转率 × 杠杆 差距，几乎全在最后一项 比亚迪 净利率 4.06% × 总资产周转 0.91 × 权益乘数 3.42 = ROE 12.61% 特斯拉 净利率 4.00% × 总资产周转 0.69 × 权益乘数 1.67 = ROE 4.62% 🔍 一项一项看，真相出来了 净利率：几乎一样 （4.06% vs 4.00%）。 周转率：比亚迪略胜 （0.91 vs 0.69）。 权益乘数（杠杆）：3.42 vs 1.67，差一倍多 —— ROE 那 2.7 倍的差距，几乎全是这一项撑出来的。 不是比亚迪更会赚钱，是它用了更高的杠杆。 杠杆这么高 → 那它危险吗？↓ 观众一定会问 杠杆 3.42 倍—— 那比亚迪是不是很危险？ 关键不是杠杆多高，是这杠杆"欠的是谁的钱" 应付账款（无息·占供应商的钱） 2,092亿 经营负债，利息为零 有息负债（真欠银行的） 1,245亿 仅占总负债的一小截 🔍 经营杠杆 ≠ 金融杠杆 比亚迪的高杠杆， 大头是应付账款（2,092 亿）——占用供应商的钱、不付利息 ，是"规模大、供应商离不开我"的 议价能力 ；真正欠银行、要还利息的有息负债只有 1,245 亿。 所以这 3.42 倍杠杆， 高，但没有"高负债"听起来那么危险 ——它不是借钱赌博，是拿供应链的钱在转。 那不靠杠杆，比亚迪 ROE 还剩多少？↓ 做个还原实验 把杠杆拉到和特斯拉一样 比亚迪 ROE 会掉到多少？ 比亚迪（实际，杠杆3.42） 12.61% 比亚迪（假设降到杠杆1.67） ≈6.2% 特斯拉（实际，杠杆1.67） 4.62% 🔍 12.61% 里，多少是真本事？ 把比亚迪杠杆按到特斯拉水平（1.67），ROE 会从 12.61% 掉到 约 6.2% ——仍高于特斯拉 4.6%。 这剩下的约 1.3 倍，才是它真实的效率优势（更快的资产周转）。 所以 2.7 倍的表面差距里， 大约一半是杠杆"放大镜"，另一半才是真功夫。 那特斯拉 ROE 才 4.6%，是它差吗？↓ 另一个追问 特斯拉 ROE 只有 4.6%—— 是它不会赚钱吗？ 🔍 不是差，是"选择" + "估值后遗症" ① 主动低杠杆： 手里趴着约 3,000 亿现金 没用足，负债率才 39.87%。不是借不到钱，是不想加杠杆——安全，但 ROE 自然被压低。 ② 分母被撑大： ROE = 净利 ÷ 净资产 。特斯拉常年高估值融资，净资产高达 5,594 亿（比亚迪只有 2,586 亿）。分母大，ROE 就显得低。 所以低 ROE 是它"保守 + 高估值"的结果，不等于经营不行。 先别急着下结论 → 看一眼最新一季 ↓ 别只看年报快照 但 2026 一季度—— 故事正在 反转 比亚迪 2026Q1 归母净利 40.9亿 同比 −55.4% · 营收 −11.8% 特斯拉 2026Q1 净利 $477M 同比 +16.6% · 营收 +16% 🔍 那个 2.7 倍的 ROE 优势，正在缩水 FY2025 的 12.61% vs 4.62% 是" 过去式 "。进入 2026 第一季： 比亚迪净利腰斩（−55%） ，特斯拉反而 回升（+17%） 。把 Q1 年化，比亚迪 ROE 从 12.6% 滑到约 6.5% ，特斯拉升到约 2.3% —— 优势在快速收窄。ROE 不能只看年报快照，得看趋势。 季度 ROE = Q1 净利 ÷ 期末净资产 再简单 ×4 年化，仅看趋势方向，非精确值。 所以这块"砖"，砌的是哪座"楼"？↓ PM 视角 · 这块砖砌哪座楼 ROE 能比大小， 但"高 ROE 的含义"完全不同 🏦 比亚迪：用别人的钱（无息占款）把 ROE 做到 12.61%，是制造业的极致玩法——高效，但依赖规模与议价权。特斯拉：守着现金、低杠杆，ROE 只有 4.62%——安全，但资本没榨干。 🧱 它支撑的判断（楼）：财务韧性 同样一个"12.61% vs 4.62%"，PM 读出的不是"谁更会赚钱"，而是 两种完全不同的财务体质 ：一个把杠杆玩到极致、跑得快但绷得紧；一个躺在现金上、慢但稳。 结论：ROE 能比大小，但不能直接说"比亚迪强 2.7 倍"——拆开才知道，一半是杠杆放大，一半才是真效率，而且这优势正被 Q1 的利润下滑侵蚀。 💡 看 ROE 永远别只看那个数多大—— 要拆开问一句：它是怎么来的？ 这一问，就是普通人和分析师的分水岭。 拆解上市公司 · 有二财经 结语 数据来源：比亚迪 2025 年报（分部附注：汽车及相关分部 6,483.93亿/5,156.03亿→20.48%；研发投入634.41亿、资本化率8.61%）、特斯拉 2025 10-K（汽车分部收入$69,526M，包括车销售$65,821M+租赁$1,712M+碳积分$1,993M；汽车毛利$12,361M/$69,526M=17.8%，剔碳积分≈15.3%；研发$6,411M；总营收$94,827M；净利$3,785M）。汇率 6.8109（2026.6.15）。本内容仅作教育研究用途，不构成任何投资建议。 拆解上市公司 · 有二财经

赛力斯，是谁的赛力斯？ 1 / 9 中国汽车史上最魔幻的一场翻身仗 赛力斯，是谁的赛力斯？ 五年前差点破产的面包车厂，今天卖着50万的豪车—— 但很多人说，主角不是它 濒临绝境 2021年以前 东风小康面包车起家 转型电动车无人问津，连年亏损 1,650亿 2025年营收 问界一年交付42.6万辆 50万以上市场，每10辆有7辆是M9 华为 翻身的另一个名字 车是赛力斯造的 但座舱、智驾、门店、光环……是谁的？ 要回答"是谁的"，先看它姓什么——从股权和出身说起 → 2 / 9 先认识它：一家重庆公司的四次转身 它的前半生，三次都差点没挺过去 创始人张兴海——重庆人， 做弹簧出身 1986 做弹簧 汽车座椅弹簧 零部件小厂 → 2003 造面包车 与东风合资"东风小康" 微车卖到全国前三 → 2016 赌电动车 金康SF5 市场反应惨淡，连年亏损 → 2021 抱华为 全行业怕"失去灵魂"不敢接 它接了——问界诞生 ≈25% 张兴海家族（小康控股系） 第一大股东，但远谈不上一手遮天 18.79% 东风汽车集团 · 第二大股东 央企坐在董事会里 连股权都是"合作"的底色 上一期的长城，是把全部身家押在自己车上；赛力斯不一样，它天生是"借力"的命。借力借出了什么成绩？ → 股权数据：2026年一季报前十大股东（小康控股20.98%+渝安汽车3.79%等） 3 / 9 2021年它接了全行业不敢接的方案，四年后—— 这场翻身仗打得有多狠？ 从面包车到50万豪车， 三项纪录 说明一切 42.6万辆 2025年问界交付量 M9超11万 · M8超15万 · M7超11万 国内销量最高的中国豪华品牌 28.8% 新能源车毛利率 · 新势力第一 比特斯拉高，比理想高 2022年这个数字还只有8% 46个月 第100万辆下线用时 新势力最快纪录 理想58个月、蔚来91个月 💡 对比一下才知道多夸张 2022年8月，问界累计销量还 不到3万辆 ； 2025年，它一年卖 42.6万辆 ，营收1,650亿，净利润59.6亿，连续两年盈利—— 全球第四家盈利的新能源车企。 成绩单很漂亮。但把账本翻开，每一页都写着同一个名字 → 数据来源：赛力斯2025年报、公司官方发布；毛利率为新能源汽车业务口径（审计数据） 4 / 9 账本第一问：卖一辆39万的车，自己留多少？ 钱的真相：大头不归它 毛利率全行业第一，净利率只有 3.6% ——中间的钱去哪了？ 一辆问界卖出去 均价约39万 流向华为体系的采购 约13.6万 赛力斯最后留下的净利 约1.4万 💡 13.6万买的是什么？ 两样东西： 零部件 （鸿蒙座舱、智驾系统）+ 服务 （华为约700家门店帮它卖车、做推广）。 注意：招股书写明双方 没有利润分成 ——华为赚的是"卖货+服务"的钱， 但三年半下来，赛力斯累计向华为采购了 750亿 。 钱给出去还能挣回来。真正的问题是：除了钱，命脉也在别人手里 → 13.6万=2025上半年向华为采购200亿÷同期交付14.7万辆（港股招股书披露，测算值）；1.4万=2025归母净利59.6亿÷交付42.6万辆（测算值） 净利率3.6%=59.6亿÷1650.5亿 5 / 9 账本第二问：哪些东西不是自己的？ 命脉的三个依赖 技术、渠道、品牌—— 车企最值钱的三样 ，都和华为深度绑定 🧠 技术靠引望 座舱+智驾 问界最大的卖点——鸿蒙座舱和驾驶辅助，核心技术在华为系的引望手里。自家研发在猛追，但今天的招牌菜还是别人掌勺。 🏪 渠道靠华为门店 约700家 问界主要在华为运营的体验中心展示、试驾、成交。等于把"销售命门"放在合作方的店里——店是别人的，客流也是别人的。 ✨ 品牌靠光环，且在稀释 72% 买问界，很大程度是买"华为"。但鸿蒙智行已集齐"五界"——问界在体系内的销量占比，从当年的绝对主力降到了72%，不再是独宠。 赛力斯自己清楚这三条命脉的分量——所以这两年它在干一件事：花钱赎身 → 问界占鸿蒙智行销量比例为2025年数据（公开报道）；招股书风险提示原文承认对主要供应商存在重大依赖 6 / 9 最有意思的部分来了 一边赎身，一边绑得更紧 看起来矛盾，其实是同一个策略： 别把命运交给运气 25亿 买回"问界"商标 919项商标+44项专利从华为手里买断 名字先变成自己的 115亿 入股引望10% 从"华为的客户"变成"华为车BU的股东" 桌子对面坐到了桌子同侧 125亿 2025年研发投入 +77% 2022年才13亿，三年翻近10倍 港股募的140亿，七成也投研发 💡 怎么理解这套组合拳 买商标、堆研发，是怕华为哪天 不带它玩 ； 花115亿入股引望，是确保华为 继续带它玩 。 两头下注，这不是摇摆——是一家被命运吓过一次的公司，在买保险。 赎身要花钱，钱会先砸出坑。这个坑，在2026年一季报里清清楚楚 → 港股2025年11月上市，募资净额140.16亿港元，约70%投研发（招股书）；引望股权2025年完成全部交割 7 / 9 2026年一季报：收入大涨，利润却"见了底" 营收+34%，真实利润只剩1个亿？ 没有造假，没有暴雷——是 赎身的账单到了 指标 Q1 2026 人话版 营业收入 +34% 257亿 车卖得很好，生意没问题 归母净利润 +0.9% 7.5亿 看着平稳？往下看—— 其中：政府补助等非经常收益 6.5亿 7.5亿利润里，6.5亿不是卖车赚的 扣非净利润 -74% 1.03亿 主业真实利润——被研发吃掉了：研发费用单季17.9亿，比去年多花7.4亿 经营现金流 -210亿 巨额流出 季报解释：收车款的速度赶不上给供应商付款的速度。规模吓人，需要连续盯几个季度 💡 一句话判断 这份季报是 "赎身计划"的成本侧 ：研发翻倍把利润吃薄，是它自己选的。 真正要警惕的不是利润薄，而是 利润对政府补助的依赖 和 现金流的连续性 。 投入期能不能熬过去，看产品接不接得住。2026年下半年，盯三件事 → 1-5月新能源销量14.5万辆、同比+15%——还在涨，但和营收+34%的预期比不算快。M6（25-30万级）要来填M5和M7之间的空档，走量靠它。 ⚔️ "五界"内战怎么打？ 华为的亲儿子越来越多，问界从独宠变成五分之一。资本市场已经在重新定价：港股上市后市值一度蒸发数百亿。华为光环还值多少钱，市场正在投票。 最后，把这十分钟收进三个数字 → 来源：公司公告、月度销量快报、公开报道（2026年4-6月） 9 / 9 回到开头：赛力斯，是谁的赛力斯？ 记住这三个数字， 你就看懂了赛力斯 28.8% 毛利率，新势力第一 翻身仗是真的赢了—— 抱大腿抱出了全行业最好的身板 13.6万 每辆车流向华为的采购 身板是自己的 但心脏起搏器在别人手里 265亿 赎身的总投入 25亿买商标+115亿入股引望+125亿研发 它在把"借来的命"变成自己的 长安汽车 · 真正的压力并不在于负债 长安汽车 · 深度拆解 真正的压力 并不在于负债 2025年报 + 2026一季报数据全景 Part 1 · 负债 负债端：看似危险，实则安全 2026年一季度末资产负债表关键数据 398亿 货币资金 一季度末账上现金 57.1% 资产负债率 1907亿总资产 · 1090亿总负债 23.3倍 现金/(借款+债券) 借款+债券17.1亿 · 现金398亿 17.1亿 借款+债券 短借0.44亿+一年内到期6.71亿+债券10亿 &#128161; 长安的负债大头是应付票据和应付账款（对上游供应商的占款），而不是银行借款。借款和债券合计仅17.1亿（短期借款0.44亿+一年内到期6.71亿+应付债券10亿），398亿现金对应17.1亿借款和债券，几乎不靠银行贷款。 Part 2 · 合资联营 合资联营：销量与投资收益双杀 福特 · 马自达 · 阿维塔 · 2025.1 — 2026.5 月度销量 合资联营板块月度销量 阿维塔 · 长安马自达 · 长安福特 · 单位：辆 Part 2 · 投资收益 联营合营投资收益：Q4断崖下跌 "对联营企业和合营企业的投资收益" · 各季度单季数据（亿元） 联营合营企业投资收益（单季） 2025Q1 — 2026Q1 · 阿维塔2025年确认投资亏损12.12亿，Q4集中体现 ⚠️ 2025全年对联营合营企业投资收益为-4.3亿（2024年为+3.7亿）。Q4单季亏损5.70亿，主要来自阿维塔的投资亏损确认。福特、马自达销量也在持续萎缩。 Part 3 · 自营销量 自营品牌：有涨有跌，价格战侵蚀毛利 引力 · 启源 · 深蓝 · 凯程 · 2025.1 — 2026.5 自营板块月度销量 单位：辆 · 虚线为基于年报反推的月度均摊值 &#128176; 2025年单车均价降至5.63万元（2024年为5.96万），海外均价从6.05万降至5.21万。价格战导致毛利率承压——国内毛利率下降、海外毛利率从26.2%降至19.5%。 Part 4 · 毛利率 综合毛利率：逐季改善后，2026Q1回落 2025Q1 — 2026Q1 · 价格战下毛利率承压 综合毛利率季度趋势 2025全年毛利率15.54%（同比+0.6pp）· 季度逐季向上至Q4的16.82% · 2026Q1回落至14.08% &#128200; 2025年毛利率逐季走高（13.86%→15.2%→15.7%→16.82%），新能源规模效应+供应链降本推动改善。但2026Q1回落至14.08%，受价格战和淡季影响。国内毛利率约14%，海外毛利率19.49%，海外高出5个百分点。 Part 5 · 出口 出口：唯一亮点，但也面临以价换量 2025.1 — 2026.5 月度出口销量 · 单位：辆 海外出口月度销量 2025全年出口63.7万辆（+18.85%）· 2026年1-5月出口35.6万辆 &#127758; 出口是唯一正增长的板块，但海外毛利率从26.2%降至19.5%。2026年Q1受汇兑损失影响，财务费用同比多出13亿。以价换量的模式能否持续，需要观察。 Part 6 · 现金流 现金流：2026Q1经营现金流转负 经营活动现金流净额 · 各季度单季数据（亿元） 经营活动现金流净额（单季） 2025Q1 — 2026Q1 &#128184; 2025年全年经营现金流净额18.36亿（正），但2026Q1急转直下至-116.47亿。合资联营在跌、自营有涨有跌、唯一好的是出口——但出口也在以价换量。现金流压力可能还会加大。 Part 7 · 应付票据 应付票据占比飙升至74% 应付票据 /（应付票据+应付账款）· 2025Q1 — 2026Q1 应付票据与应付账款结构变化 单位：亿元 · 柱状图为绝对值 · 折线为票据占比 ⚠️ 2026Q1应付票据494.81亿，占应付票据+应付账款之和的74.2%。应付票据比应付账款对上游供应商的压力更大——票据有明确的到期日，到期必须兑付，不像应付账款可以协商延期。 &#128221; 本分析基于公开财报及相关数据，仅为个人意见，不构成投资建议。所有数据均来源于公司定期报告、乘联会及公开媒体报道，旨在提供一个严谨的分析视角供投资者参考。 数据说明 数据来源与口径说明 负债/现金流数据 来自长安汽车2025年一季报、半年报、三季报、年报及2026年一季报合并财务报表。借款+债券=短期借款+一年内到期的非流动负债+应付债券。 毛利率 2025Q1=13.86%、Q2=15.2%（券商研报及半年报验证）、Q3=15.7%（三季报）、Q4=16.82%（年报），2026Q1=14.08%（一季报）。海外毛利率19.49%，国内毛利率约14%。 合资联营销量 阿维塔来自官方产销快报及媒体报道；福特/马自达2025.1-5月来自官方产销快报，6-12月来自乘联会零售数据。 自营品牌销量 引力/凯程部分月份基于年报全年数据反推均摊（虚线标识）；深蓝/启源全部有实测数据。 出口销量 2025年部分月份基于年报全年63.7万辆反推均摊（虚线标识）；2026年1-5月全部有实测数据。 投资收益 各季度"对联营企业和合营企业的投资收益"来自合并利润表。阿维塔2025年确认投资亏损12.12亿。

重新认识吉利汽车 · 有二财经 1 / 8 它让旗下一家上市公司 上市不到两年就退市了 手上捏着四五个品牌 二十年来满世界买买买 买过的品牌，比大多数车企拥有的还多 本内容不构成投资建议 · 数据来源：吉利汽车公告及公开报道 2 / 8 这家车企，就是 吉利 下面八页，从头拆一遍：买 → 用 → 合 → 兑现 银河 + 吉利 + 领克 + 极氪 手上四五个品牌 银河新能源主力 / 吉利燃油基盘 领克中高端 / 极氪高端纯电 302万辆 年销量 中国第二家年销300万辆的车企 20+年 全球收购史 从18亿美元吞沃尔沃 到90亿美元入股奔驰 先讲 买 和 用 ——这些品牌和技术，是怎么来的 3 / 8 故事一 · 买，是为了用 二十年，满世界收 吉利和其他中国车企最大的不同： 它买来的东西，后来都用什么了 2010 收购沃尔沃轿车 100% 股权 18亿美元 + 9亿运营资金 2010年3月，吉利以 18亿美元 从福特手中收购沃尔沃轿车 100%股权 及全部知识产权。当时吉利年营收140多亿人民币，沃尔沃2007年营收106亿美元——"蛇吞象"。 买来干什么用： 不是买个品牌摆在货架上。吉利要的是沃尔沃的 安全技术体系、CMA整车架构、全球供应链管理 。今天领克的核心技术底座、银河系列部分车型的平台，根源都在这笔收购。沃尔沃是"买技术"——这是后来所有品牌能打的基础。 后续变化： 吉利已三次减持沃尔沃汽车股份套现超 43亿美元 ，远超当年27亿美元投入，但仍持有 78.7%股权、96.7%投票权 ，绝对控股未变。2026年2月沃尔沃因EX30电池召回、2025年营业利润暴跌99%导致股价大跌，吉利反手增持584万股。 2017 收购宝腾 49.9% + 路特斯 51% 未单独披露 2017年6月，吉利收购马来西亚 宝腾汽车49.9%股权 和英国 路特斯跑车51%股权 。 买来干什么用： 宝腾是马来西亚最大国有车企，拥有东南亚生产基地和完整经销网络——吉利借此 真正落地东南亚 ，这是所有中国车企里唯一做到深度的。路特斯是英国传奇跑车品牌，收购后独立上市（路特斯科技 LOT，纳斯达克），定位高端纯电和超跑，补齐了吉利在"豪华性能"一端的品牌矩阵。 2018 入股戴姆勒（奔驰母公司） 约90亿美元 2018年2月，吉利出资约 90亿美元 ，收购戴姆勒集团 9.69% 有表决权股份，一度成为最大单一股东。 买来干什么用： 不是要控股奔驰，是要 合作 。入股的直接成果是2019年 smart品牌合资 ：吉利与奔驰各持股50%，将smart从燃油微型车全面转型为纯电品牌，由中国制造返销欧洲。这是"买股权换合作"——用资本换一个高端小车的全球合作平台。 后续变化： 2023年出售戴姆勒卡车6.3%股份套现约 15亿欧元 。2026年6月美国"外国对手资本"法案生效，中国资本在车企持股合计不得超过15%——北汽9.98% + 吉利9.69% = 19.67%，触发监管红线，双方正在寻求解决方案。 2025→26 收购雷达汽车（新能源皮卡） 约2.18亿人民币 2026年5月15日完成交易，合计约 2.18亿人民币 收购雷达汽车全部股权及泰国子公司。 买来干什么用： 雷达是 新能源皮卡 品牌，2025年全年销量1.304万辆，连续三年居新能源皮卡市占率第一，纯电皮卡市占率最高达98%。收购后将皮卡品类正式纳入吉利产品矩阵——这是吉利在 商用车+户外场景 的补充，和其他品牌不重叠。 2026.5 收购福特西班牙工厂装配线 未披露 2026年5月，吉利收购福特西班牙瓦伦西亚工厂的 Body 3车身装配线 。该产线此前生产蒙迪欧、S-Max等车型，目前已闲置。 买来干什么用： 在这条产线上使用自研的 GEA全球智能新能源架构 生产紧凑型电动车，精准切入欧洲城市市场。同时 规避欧盟对中国电动车最高45.3%的关税 。更值得关注的是，福特可能基于吉利的GEA平台推出合作车型——十六年后，吉利和福特再次同框，但角色换了：2010年是"蛇吞象"的买方，今天是 输出技术标准和制造体系 的一方。 2026.5 竞购日产墨西哥COMPAS工厂 竞购中 日产因全球战略收缩，将于2026年关闭位于墨西哥阿瓜斯卡连特斯州的 COMPAS工厂 ——年产能 23万辆 ，拥有成熟技术工人和供应链配套。 买来干什么用： 通过墨西哥本地化生产 规避美国25%关税 和潜在进口限制，为进入北美市场铺路。最终竞购名单中， 吉利、比亚迪、广汽 三家中国车企入围。这是吉利在 "买全球"之后，开始"卖全球" 的关键一步——不只是把车卖到海外，而是在海外造、海外卖。 2025年交付 59.66万 +103.1% · 新势力第一 2025年营收 647.3亿 +101.3% 2025年净利润 +5.38亿 首次全年盈利 · 新势力年度盈利 单车净利 902元 卖10万的车，每辆净赚一部手机 创始人是谁？朱江明——大华股份联合创始人，做安防监控起家，摄像头做到全球第二。2015年在西班牙街头看到电动车，决定造车。他想得很简单：大华在电子制造上的积累，为什么不能搬到汽车上？ 3 / 7 2015年西班牙街头 改变了他的人生轨迹 在瓦伦西亚看到满街的雷诺电动车，朱江明决定：把造智能硬件的逻辑，用到造车上 2001 朱江明联合创办大华技术 安防监控，从零做到全球第二。核心能力：芯片、算法、硬件全自研，把成本压到极致——这套逻辑，后来直接搬进了造车。 2015 零跑汽车成立 朱江明在西班牙瓦伦西亚看到雷诺电动车，决定把大华的电子制造经验搬到汽车上。别人造车先搞发动机、底盘，零跑先搞智能驾驶芯片、中央集成式电子架构——用造智能硬件的逻辑来造车。 2019 首款量产车S01交付 不被看好，年销仅千台。但自研路线没动摇——八合一电驱、CTC电池底盘一体化，这些后来成为核心竞争力的技术，这时候已经在啃了。 2023—2025 C系列爆量，全年盈利 C11、C16连续爆款，"半价理想"外号传开。2025年全年交付59.66万台，净利润5.38亿——性价比赛道，第一次有人赚到了钱。 大华做了20年电子制造，知道怎么在薄利里抠利润。零跑把这套基因带进了造车——这是它和"汽车人创业"最根本的区别。 4 / 7 "性价比"三个字 在汽车行业等于"薄利" 零跑外号"半价理想"——配置接近理想，价格卖一半。 它怎么在别人赚不到钱的赛道里，把钱赚到了？ 答案在大华基因里：核心零部件65%自研自造。别人外采，它自产——省掉Tier1的中间利润，成本压到行业做不到的低。 环节 零跑的做法 2025年数据 造车成本 八合一电驱、CTC电池底盘一体化、智驾芯片——65%整车成本来自自研零部件 毛利率14.5% 2024年才8.4% 研发效率 只投"今天能装上车"的东西，不做远期概念 42.9亿 单车约7,200元 渠道效率 不重金铺直营，靠性价比口碑走量 销售费率5.6% 行业偏低 出海成本 不烧钱建海外渠道——借Stellantis的网卖车，"反向合资" 出口6.7万台 新势力出口第一 来源：65%自研自造——公司2025年报及2026Q1公告；毛利率14.5%（2024年8.4%）——2025年报；研发42.9亿、销售费率5.6%——2025年报管理层讨论与分析；出口67,052台——2025年报 5 / 7 但2026年Q1 这份成绩单让人皱眉 销量在涨、营收在涨， 利润重新见红，毛利率大幅下滑 指标 2026年Q1 对比 营收 108.2亿 +8.0% 销量 110,155台 +25.8%（量升，但均价在降） 毛利率 9.4% 去年同期14.9% / 上季度15.0% 归母净利润 -3.9亿 由盈转亏 经营现金流 -66.1亿 2025全年为+126.2亿 在手资金 306.3亿 单季减少约72亿，安全垫仍厚 毛利率从15%跌到9.4%——公司公告解释两点：①低价车（B系列+A10）占比上升；②对Stellantis的技术授权收入（高毛利）Q1缩量。量在涨、价在降、高毛利副业在缩——这三件事碰在一起，Q1的亏损就不意外了。 来源：营收108.2亿（+8.0%）、毛利率9.4%及归因原文、净亏3.9亿、经营现金流-66.1亿、在手306.3亿——零跑2026Q1业绩公告（2026.5.15） 6 / 7 Q1的裂缝，4月开始补 连续上了三款新车—— 走量的基本盘没松，第一次把车价摸到20万以上 A10 10万内首搭激光雷达 3月26日上市 首月大定超4万台 D19 21.98—26.98万 · 旗舰SUV 4月16日上市 · 零跑第一次卖过20万 15天大定超1.5万台 D99 旗舰MPV · 6月25日预售 车长超5.2米，增程+纯电双动力，7月上市交付。继续往上打价格带。 4月交付 71,387 破新势力月销纪录 · 同比+73.9% 5月交付 81,569 新势力首个破8万 · 同比+81% Q1出口 40,901台 同比+442% · 占销量37.1% 关键问题：A10卖得越多，毛利率压力越大。D19/D99能不能把均价和毛利拉回来？这道算术题，Q3财报会给出第一个答案。 来源：A10 48小时订单破万、首月大定4万+——2026Q1公告；D19 15天大定1.5万——新华网；4月71,387台、5月81,569台——公司交付公告；Q1出口40,901台（+442%）——2026Q1公告 7 / 7 零跑，往后盯三件事 1 D19/D99能不能把均价拉起来？ "半价理想"的外号是流量，也是天花板。D平台能不能让零跑摘掉"性价比"的帽子，Q3财报第一个见分晓。均价每涨1万，对利润的影响比多卖1万台车还大。 2 出口能不能稳住月均3万台以上？ Q1出口占销量37.1%，欧洲16国上牌同比+726.5%，意大利拿下了纯电销冠。反向合资不走烧钱路线，但Stellantis的合作收入Q1在缩量——这块高毛利业务能不能回来，直接影响毛利率。 3 100万辆×50亿，军令状能不能交？ 管理层目标：2026年销量100万辆、净利润50亿。Q1亏3.9亿，后三季度要补约54亿。单车净利要从902元跳到5,000元——一年翻5.5倍。1-5月完成26.3%，销量端月均8万+够得到，但利润端才是真正的考点。Q3是全年最关键季度：D19/D99规模交付+出口旺季，如果单车净利能摸到2,000-3,000元，军令状就还在轨道上。 朱江明从大华出来，把电子制造的成本逻辑带进了造车。在最难赚钱的赛道里，他把钱赚到了。接下来看的是：他能不能在更高的价格带上，再做一次。 来源：零跑汽车2025年报（经审计）、2026Q1业绩公告、2026年4-6月交付公告 100万辆/50亿目标——2025年报电话会，副总裁李腾飞"净利润目标维持50亿元不变"（每日经济新闻2026-03-17） 本内容为公司公开信息分析，不构成投资建议

单车净利 902元 ——差不多一部手机。但它真的赚到了 65%的整车成本来自自研零部件 → 省掉Tier1中间利润 → 14.5%的毛利率就是这么来的 环节 零跑的做法 2025数据 造车成本 八合一电驱、CTC电池底盘一体化——65%核心零部件自研自造 毛利率14.5% 2024年才8.4% 研发 只投"今天能装上车的东西"——不做远期概念 42.9亿 单车约7,200元 销售 不重金铺直营店——靠性价比口碑走量 36.5亿 费率5.6% 副产品 碳积分交易——出口带来的收入 27.2亿 +413% 同一道算术题：卖贵的反而不赚钱？ 零跑单车净利902元，全年净赚5.38亿。对照：蔚来卖30多万的车，至今还在亏。 创始人朱江明做了三十年电子制造——把造摄像头的成本逻辑搬进了造车。 国内这套打法通了。出口呢？ 它走了一条没人走过的路 → 来源：65%自研自造——公司2025年报及2026Q1公告原文；研发42.9亿（+47.9%）、销售36.5亿（+70.6%）、服务及其他27.2亿（+413.2%）——2025年报管理层讨论与分析 3 / 7 出 海 策 略 不自己烧钱建海外渠道 让外国巨头掏钱替你卖 全行业独一份： 反向合资 2023年Stellantis投约15亿欧元入股约20% → 2024年成立"零跑国际"，外方出钱出渠道、中方出车出技术 → 四十年前老外来中国合资要技术，这次反过来了 +442% Q1出口增速 40,901台，占总销量37.1% +726.5% 欧洲16国上牌增速 2.33万台 · 意大利纯电销冠 约1,000家 海外网点 欧洲超850家 · 几乎没花自己的钱 关键逻辑 2025全年出口67,052台——新势力出口第一。2026年2月累计出口已破10万台。 不烧钱建渠道＝不用为出口拖累利润，这在所有出海的新势力里是独一份。 国内赚钱、海外省钱，看起来很完美。但 一季报上出了问题 → 来源：Stellantis投资约15亿欧元获约20%股权（2023-10公告）；Q1出口40,901台（+442%、占37.1%）、欧洲16国上牌2.33万台（+726.5%）、海外网点约1,000家——零跑2026Q1业绩公告 4 / 7 2026 年 一 季 报 Q1利润重回亏损，钱在加速流出 收入在涨、销量在涨， 利润却重新见红 毛利率从15%掉到9.4%，经营现金流-66.1亿，单季现金净减72亿 —— 薄利模式最怕"量上去、利下来" 指标 2026年Q1 对比 营收 108.2亿 +8.0% 销量 110,155台 +25.8%（量升价跌） 毛利率 9.4% 同期14.9% / 上季15.0% 净利润 -3.9亿 由盈转亏 经营现金流 -66.1亿 2025全年为+126.2亿 在手资金 306.3亿 单季减72亿，仍较充裕 分清两类问题 现金流为负 ：公司公告原文解释——"账期节奏带来的到期应付款项加大"。2025全年现金流是+126.2亿，Q1是季节性低谷，可修复。 毛利率掉5.5个点 ：低价车占比上升 + 战略合作业务减少。这是结构性问题，需要盯。 公司自己显然知道问题出在哪。4月以后 上了两个新变量 → 来源：收入108.2亿（+8.0%）、毛利率9.4%（同期14.9%）及归因原文、净亏3.9亿、经营现金流-66.1亿、在手306.3亿——零跑2026Q1业绩公告 5 / 7 新 变 量 量再上台阶，价往上够 低价走量稳基本盘，第一次把车卖过 20万 ——修毛利率 8.16万 5月交付（+81%） 新势力首个破8万 21.98万起 旗舰D19 · 4月16日上市 15天大定超15,000辆 D99 旗舰MPV 6月预售 · 7月上市交付 走量底盘没松：A10（10万内首搭激光雷达）首月大定超4万；Lafa5车系3个月破2万 —— 低价基本盘牢固 还有个伏笔 2025年12月与中国一汽签了内资股认购协议——国家队入场。不仅是钱，更意味着供应链和渠道资源。 条件都齐了。最后看管理层的 军令状 → 来源：5月81,569台——公司交付公告；D19上市15天大定1.5万+（21.98-26.98万）；A10首月大定4万+——零跑2026Q1业绩公告；一汽2025-12-28内资股认购协议 6 / 7 2026 年 目 标 100万辆 × 5,000元 = 50亿 管理层立的军令状，至今没改口： 销量100万辆、净利润50亿 2025年实际单车净利902元 → 2026年目标单车5,000元 → 一年之内翻5.5倍。销量端不难，利润端才是考点 验证维度 当前进度 关键观察节点 销量：100万辆 1-5月已交付约26.3万台（26.3%） 5月已月销8万+，下半年月均9万+够得着 利润：50亿 Q1亏损3.9亿 看Q3（D19、D99大规模交付+出口旺季） 毛利率修复 Q1仅9.4% 看半年报毛利率是否回到13%+ 现金流 在手306.3亿（Q1减72亿） 看Q2经营现金流是否回正 最后，记住三个关键数字 → 来源：100万辆/50亿目标——2025年报业绩电话会，副总裁李腾飞"净利润目标维持50亿元不变"（每日经济新闻2026-03-17）；1-5月约26.3万台＝Q1 110,155＋4月71,387＋5月81,569 7 / 7 总 结 零跑的三个核心数字 自研占比 65% 整车成本中自研零部件占比 便宜还能赚钱的根基 单车净利 902元 2025年实际水平 薄利模式的真相 目标单车净利 5,000元 2026年军令状要求 需翻5.5倍 65%（根基）→ 902元（现状）→ 5,000元（目标）。这三个数之间的跨度，就是零跑2026年要交的答卷 三点判断 1. 成本控制是真实力 ：65%自研 + 5.6%销售费率，别人复制不了 2. 反向合资是护城河 ：出口不烧钱、还赚碳积分，新势力独一份 3. 50亿军令状是压力测试 ：D19/D99能否拉均价、毛利率能否回15%，是2026年最关键的两个问题 来源：零跑汽车2025年报（经审计）、2026Q1业绩公告、2026年4-6月交付公告 本内容为公司公开信息分析，不构成投资建议

KEY INFORMATION Our Holding Company Structure and Contractual Arrangements with the VIEs NIO Inc. is not an operating company in China but a Cayman Islands holding company with no equity ownership in its consolidated variable interest entities, or VIEs. We conduct our operations in China (i) primarily through our PRC subsidiaries, and (ii) to a much lesser extent, through the VIEs, namely Beijing NIO, Anhui NIO AT, and Anhui NIO DT, with each of which we maintain contractual arrangements, and their subsidiary. We have also established subsidiaries in the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, Norway and other overseas jurisdictions to promote our services and businesses, enter into business contracts with offshore counterparties and hold overseas intellectual properties. PRC laws and regulations (i) restrict and impose conditions on foreign investment in value-added telecommunication services, including without limitation, performing internet information services and holding certain related licenses; and (ii) prohibit foreign investment in certain services related to autonomous driving as well as the holding of related licenses by foreign entities. Additionally, in practice, subject to the qualifications set by China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (currently known as the National Administration of Financial Regulation) for foreign shareholders of the insurance brokerage companies, the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission typically would not approve the establishment of a foreign-invested insurance brokerage company to perform insurance brokerage services and hold certain related licenses. We operate these businesses in China through Beijing NIO, Anhui NIO AT, and Anhui NIO DT, or as referred to as the VIEs, and NIO Insurance Broker Co., Ltd., the subsidiary of Anhui NIO DT. We rely on contractual arrangements among our PRC subsidiaries, the VIEs and their nominee shareholders to maintain a controlling financial interest as the primary beneficiary of each VIE (as defined in U.S. GAAP, ASC 810). Under U.S. GAAP, we consolidate each VIE within our consolidated financial statements. Specifically, we operate value-added telecommunication services, including without limitation, performing internet information services, and hold certain related licenses, through Beijing NIO. We rely on the contractual arrangements with Anhui NIO DT and its shareholders to operate insurance brokerage services. NIO Insurance Broker Co., Ltd. currently holds an insurance brokerage license and provides insurance brokerage services primarily related to vehicles and properties. We intend to obtain requisite licenses for certain supporting functions during the development of our assisted and intelligent driving technology through Anhui NIO AT. As of the date of this annual report, the business operations of the VIEs are insignificant in relation to our total revenues and net loss. As used in this annual report, “NIO,” “we,” “us,” “our company,” and “our” refer to NIO Inc., our Cayman Islands holding company and its subsidiaries, and in the context of describing our operations and consolidated financial information, include the VIEs and NIO Insurance Broker Co., Ltd., the subsidiary of Anhui NIO DT. 4 Table of Contents The following diagram illustrates our corporate structure, including our principal subsidiaries and the VIEs, as of the date of this annual report: Note: (1) Upon completion of an ongoing investment transaction, NIO Technology (Anhui) Co. Risk Factors—Risks Related to Doing Business in China—We may be adversely affected by the complexity, uncertainties and changes in PRC regulations on internet-related business, automotive businesses and other business carried out by our PRC subsidiaries and the VIEs.” Meanwhile, the PRC government has sought to exert more oversight and control over capital raising activities of listed companies that are conducted overseas and/or foreign investment in China-based issuers. In December 2021, the Cyberspace Administration of China, or the CAC, together with other authorities, jointly promulgated the Cybersecurity Review Measures, which took effect on February 15, 2022 and replaces its predecessor regulation. Pursuant to the Cybersecurity Review Measures, critical information infrastructure operators that procure internet products and services and network platform operators that conduct data process activities must be subject to the cybersecurity review if their activities affect or may affect national security. On February 17, 2023, China Securities Regulatory Commission, or the CSRC, released several regulations regarding the filing requirements for overseas offerings and listings by domestic companies, including the Trial Administrative Measures of Overseas Securities Offering and Listing by Domestic Companies and five supporting guidelines, which were formally implemented on March 31, 2023. According to these rules, domestic enterprises like us that have completed overseas listings are not required to file with CSRC immediately, but shall carry out filing procedures as required if we conduct refinancing or fall within other circumstances that require filing with the CSRC. Any failure to obtain or delay in obtaining such approval or completing such procedures could subject us to restrictions and penalties imposed by the CSRC, the CAC or other PRC regulatory authorities, which could include fines and penalties on our operations in China, delays of or restrictions on the repatriation of the proceeds from our offshore offerings into China, or other actions that could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects, as well as the trading price of our ADSs. For more detailed information, see “Item 3. Key Information—D. We conduct our operations in China (i) primarily through our PRC subsidiaries, and (ii) to a much lesser extent, the VIEs and their subsidiary. As a result, although other means are available for us to obtain financing at the holding company level, NIO Inc.’s ability to pay dividends to the shareholders and to service any debt it may incur may depend upon dividends paid by our PRC subsidiaries and service fees paid by the VIEs in China. If any of our subsidiaries incurs debt on its own behalf in the future, the instruments governing such debt may restrict its ability to pay dividends to NIO Inc. In addition, our PRC subsidiaries are permitted to pay dividends to NIO Inc. only out of their retained earnings, if any, as determined in accordance with PRC accounting standards and regulations. Further, our PRC subsidiaries and the VIEs are required to make appropriations to certain statutory reserve funds or may make appropriations to certain discretionary funds, which are not distributable as cash dividends except in the event of a solvent liquidation of the companies. Risk Factors.” Risks Related to Our Business and Industry Risks and uncertainties related to our business and industry include, but are not limited to, the following: ● The automotive market is highly competitive, and we face significant challenges in competing in our industry; ● Our ability to develop and manufacture vehicles of sufficient quality and appeal to customers on schedule and on a large scale is still evolving; ● We incurred significant losses and negative cash flows in the past, and may continue to record net losses and negative operating cash flows in the near future; ● We have limited experience in manufacturing vehicles at scale. Any delays in the manufacturing and launching of our products, or ramping up of our production capacity, could have a material adverse effect on our business; ● Rising international political tensions, including changes in U.S. and European international trade policies and other cross-border investment regulations, particularly with regard to China, may adversely impact our business and operating results; ● The unavailability, reduction or elimination of government and economic incentives or governmental policies which are favorable for electric vehicles and domestically produced vehicles could have a material adverse effect on our business; ● Our current or future vehicles may not perform in line with customer expectations; ● We may face challenges in providing our power solutions; ● Our services may not be generally accepted by our users. Risks Related to Our Business and Industry The automotive market is highly competitive, and we face significant challenges in competing in our industry. The automotive market, particularly the market in China, is highly competitive. Our vehicles compete with both NEV and ICE vehicles across multiple market segments. Many of our current and potential competitors have significantly greater financial, technical, engineering, manufacturing, marketing and other resources than we do, and may be able to devote greater resources to the design, development, manufacturing, promotion, sale and support of their products. Moreover, we expect competition in the China automotive market to intensify in light of increased product supply, intense price competition, reduced government subsidies, continuing globalization, and industry consolidation. Increased competition will place greater demands on, among others, product design and performance, technological innovation, pricing, product quality and safety, manufacturing efficiency, sales and marketing capabilities, service and charging options, and user satisfaction. Increasing competition may also lead to lower vehicle unit sales, higher inventory, downward pricing pressure, and margin compression, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects. ​ 12 Table of Contents Furthermore, our competitive advantages as a leading and early-moving EV company will be compromised if our competitors achieve higher production and sales volumes, offer more favorable pricing, or introduce new products or services at a faster pace than we do. If our competitors introduce new vehicles or services that successfully compete with or surpass the quality or performance of our offerings at more competitive prices, we may be unable to satisfy existing customers or attract new customers at the price levels that would allow us to generate acceptable rates of return on our investment. We may also be affected by volatility in the overall China automotive market. Fluctuations in the growth rate of passenger vehicle sales and/or EV sales and shifting consumer demands for EVs could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. Our ability to successfully compete is fundamental to our future success in existing and new markets and in growing our market share. There can be no assurance that we will be able to compete successfully. You should consider our business and prospects in light of the risks and challenges we face in our industry, including, among other things, with respect to our ability to: ● design and produce safe, reliable and high-quality vehicles on an ongoing basis; ● build and maintain a well-recognized and respected brand; ● establish, expand and retain our customer base; ● successfully market our vehicles and services; ● competitively price our products and services, and accurately anticipate vehicle sales volume and service adoption rates; ● improve and maintain our operational and cost efficiency; ● maintain a reliable, secure, high-performance and scalable technology infrastructure; ● successfully develop and protect our core technologies; ● attract , retain and motivate talented employees; ● anticipate and adapt to changing market conditions, including technological developments and changes in competitive landscape ; and ● navigate an evolving and complex regulatory environment. If we fail to address any or all of these risks and challenges, our business may be materially and adversely affected. Furthermore, our vehicles are highly technical products that will require ongoing maintenance, software updates and support. The United States and various foreign governments have imposed license requirements and restrictions on the export of technologies and products to China, or voiced the intention to do so. For instance, since 2022, the United States has imposed increasingly strict export control measures relating to exports of semiconductors to China. In October 2023, BIS promulgated two new rules that expanded export controls to cover a broader array of advanced semiconductors and semiconductor manufacturing equipment. Similarly, in January 2025, BIS released an interim final rule that established licensing requirements for the export of advanced computing integrated circuits that facilitate advanced artificial intelligence (AI) research and development, as well as certain AI model technology. In September 2025, BIS released an interim final rule that extended export restrictions to non-U.S. entities owned 50% or more, directly or indirectly, individually or in aggregate, by listed parties designated on the Entity List, the Military End User List, and under certain OFAC sanctions programs. On October 30, 2025, following a series of negotiations aimed at reducing trade tensions between the U.S. and China, the U.S. announced a one-year pause of this interim final rule, which went into effect on November 10, 2025. These recent export controls are, in part, intended to restrict China’s ability to obtain advanced computing chips, develop and maintain supercomputers, and manufacture advanced semiconductors. These measures also restrict the ability of U.S. persons to provide “support” for semiconductor manufacturing and related activities in China and may seriously affect the ability of Chinese companies to purchase or obtain certain semiconductor manufacturing equipment or advanced chips. The implementation, interpretation and impact on our business of these rules and other regulatory actions taken by the U.S. government is uncertain. These actions and/or other actions that may be taken by the governments of either the U.S. or China, or both (including in response to recent increased tensions), could hinder our ability to transfer our U.S.-origin software to China, source U.S.-origin software and components or otherwise access U.S. technology, which could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. The United States has also taken efforts to limit U.S. investment in China. On October 28, 2024, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued a final rule to prohibit U.S. investment in Chinese companies active in developing certain national security technologies (the “Outbound Investment Rule”). The Outbound Investment Rule targets investments involving persons and entities associated with “countries of concern,” a designation currently limited to China. In effect since January 2025, the Outbound Investment Rule imposes investment prohibitions and notification requirements on a range of investments in companies engaged in activities relating to three sectors: (i) semiconductors and microelectronics, (ii) quantum technologies, and (iii) artificial intelligence systems. Persons from countries of concern engaged in these activities are defined as “covered foreign persons.” Investments by U.S. persons subject to the Outbound Investment Rule include the acquisition of equity or a contingent equity interest, the provision of certain debt financing, the conversion of contingent equity interest into equity interest, involvement in a greenfield or brownfield investment, entrance into a joint venture, and the acquisition of a limited partner interest in non-U.S. pooled investment fund. Importantly, the Outbound Investment Rule excludes some investments from the scope of covered transactions, including those in publicly traded securities listed on a national stock exchange. U.S. persons’ acquisitions of publicly traded securities, such as our ADSs, will therefore be exempted from the scope of covered transactions under the Outbound Investment Rule. We believe NIO Inc. is not a “Covered Foreign Person” as defined in the Outbound Investment Rule because NIO Inc. does not engage in any “covered activity” as defined in the Outbound Investment Rule or otherwise meets the definition of Covered Foreign Persons provided in the Outbound Investment Rule. However, there is no assurance that Treasury will take the same view. If NIO Inc. is deemed to be a covered foreign person engaged in the development of specified AI technologies and services, and therefore subject to the Outbound Investment Rule, our ability to raise capital or contingent equity capital from U.S. investors would be limited and could negatively affect our stock price. As a result, our financial condition, business, results of operations and prospects could also be adversely affected. Additionally, on December 18, 2025, the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act of 2025, or the COINS Act, was signed into law. The COINS Act will keep the core of the Outbound Investment Rule unchanged while expanding its scope and coverage in certain respects. The COINS Act will not take effect until the Treasury issues new regulations (subject to notice and comment), which it must do by March 13, 2027. As such, Treasury may further amend or expand existing prohibitions and restrictions in accordance with the COINS Act. Any expansion of such prohibitions may affect us adversely. 17 Table of Contents On February 21, 2025, the White House released the “America First Investment Policy” memorandum, or the Investment Policy, which indicated that the existing Outbound Investment Rule is under review to assess whether they are sufficient to address national security risks and outlined several initiatives to restrict investments involving China. While legislative and regulatory actions are required to effect these proposed changes, the Investment Policy may expand enforcement against inbound investment from China to the United States by potentially implementing broader, sector-based restriction on PRC investments in the U.S., expanding CFIUS’ jurisdiction over greenfield investment by Chinese companies, and replacing open-ended mitigation agreements with mitigation agreements prescribing specific timeframes and concrete actions. Additionally, the Investment Policy proposes to create restrictions on U.S. investments in China additional to those already imposed under the Outbound Investment Rule, by potentially expanding industry sectors covered in sectors by existing U.S. outbound investment regulations, supplementing outbound investment restrictions with sanctions, and directing a review to suspend or terminate the 1984 United States-The People’s Republic of China Income Tax Convention. As the Investment Policy and its related legislative and regulatory proposals are still relatively new, it is unclear how these policies, and any future policies concerning investments between the U.S. and China, will be interpreted, amended and implemented by U.S. government authorities. On August 20, 2020, we introduced the Battery as a Service, or BaaS, which allows users to purchase electric vehicles and subscribe for the usage of batteries separately. If users opt to purchase a vehicle and subscribe for the battery under the BaaS, they can enjoy a deduction off the original vehicle purchase price and pay a monthly subscription fee for the battery. For each user under the BaaS model, we sell a battery to Wuhan Weineng Battery Asset Co., Ltd., or the Battery Asset Company, and the user subscribes for the usage of the battery from the Battery Asset Company. The service we provide to our users under the BaaS relies, in part, on the smooth operation of and stability and quality of service delivered by the Battery Asset Company, which we cannot guarantee. We invested in the Battery Asset Company with certain other investors since its establishment. The Battery Asset Company subsequently completed several additional financings. As of the date of this annual report, NIO China beneficially owns approximately 16.5% of the equity interests in the Battery Asset Company. As a result, we have significant influence, but not control, over the business operations of the Battery Asset Company. If it fails in delivering smooth and stable operations, we will suffer from negative customer reviews and even returns of products or services and our reputation may be materially and adversely affected. 21 Table of Contents Additionally, given that we generate a portion of our total revenues from sales of battery and provision of service to the Battery Asset Company, our results of operations and financial performance will be negatively affected if the Battery Asset Company fails to operate smoothly. The Battery Asset Company may finance the purchase of batteries through issuance of equity and debt or bank borrowing. If the Battery Asset Company is unable to obtain future financings from the Battery Asset Company Investors or other third parties to meet its operational needs, it may not be able to make payments to us for the batteries purchased from us on time, to continue purchasing batteries from us and providing them to our users through battery subscription, or to otherwise maintain its healthy and sustainable operations. On the other hand, if the Battery Asset Company bears a significant rate of customer default on its payment obligations, its results of operations and financial performance may be materially impacted, which will in turn reduce the value of our and the Battery Asset Company Investors’ investments in the Battery Asset Company. In addition, in furtherance of the BaaS, we agreed to provide a guarantee to the Battery Asset Company for the default in payment of monthly subscription fees from users, while the maximum amount of guarantee that can be claimed shall not be higher than the accumulated service fees we receive from the Battery Asset Company. As the BaaS user base is expanding, if an increased number of default occurs, our results of operations and financial performance will be negatively affected. We are required by law to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, availability and authenticity of the information of our customers, which is also essential to maintaining their confidence in our vehicles and services. We have adopted strict information security policies and deployed advanced measures to implement the policies, including, among others, advanced encryption technologies. However, advances in technology, an increased level of sophistication and diversity of our products and services, an increased level of expertise of hackers, new discoveries in the field of cryptography or others can still result in a compromise or breach of the measures that we use. If we are unable to protect our systems, and hence the information stored in our systems, from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification or destruction, such problems or security breaches could cause a loss, give rise to our liabilities to the owners of information or even subject us to fines and penalties. If users allege that we have improperly collected, used, transmitted, released or disclosed their personal information, we could face legal claims and reputational damage. In addition, we may incur significant expenses to comply with privacy, consumer protection and security standards and protocols imposed by laws, regulations, industry standards or contractual obligations, some of which may not be compatible with our existing business practice. Moreover, different PRC regulatory bodies, including the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the CAC, the Ministry of Public Security, and the State Administration for Market Regulation have enforced a variety of laws and regulations regarding cybersecurity, privacy, data protection and information security with varying standards and applications in recent years, including, among others, the PRC National Security Law, the PRC Cyber Security Law, the PRC Personal Information Protection Law, the PRC Data Security Law, the Regulations on the Protection of the Security of Critical Information Infrastructure, the Cybersecurity Review Measures, the Several Provisions on Automobile Data Security Management (Trial Implementation), the Administration Measures on Data Security in the Field of Industry and Information Technology (Trial Implementation), the Measures for the Security Assessment of Data Exit, the Measures on the Standard Contract for Cross-border Transfer of Personal Information, the Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-border Data Flows, the Implementing Rules for the Risk Assessment of Data Security in the Field of Industry and Information Technology (Trial Implementation) and the Regulation on Network Data Security Management. See “Item 4. Information on the Company—B. Business Overview—Regulations—Regulations on Internet Information Security and Privacy Protection.” The following are examples of certain recent PRC regulatory activities in this area: Data Security In July 2021, the State Council of the PRC promulgated the Regulations on the Protection of the Security of Critical Information Infrastructure took effect on September 1, 2021. Pursuant to this regulation, critical information infrastructure means key network facilities or information systems of critical industries or sectors, such as public communication and information service, energy, transportation, water conservation, finance, public services, e-government affairs and national defense science, the damage, malfunction or data leakage of which may endanger national security, people’s livelihoods and the public interest. In December 2021, the CAC, together with other authorities, jointly promulgated the Cybersecurity Review Measures, which took effect on February 15, 2022 and replaces its predecessor regulation. Pursuant to the Cybersecurity Review Measures, critical information infrastructure operators that procure internet products and services and network platform operators that conduct data process activities must be subject to the cybersecurity review if their activities affect or may affect national security. The Cybersecurity Review Measures further stipulates that network platform operators that hold personal information of over one million users shall apply with the Cybersecurity Review Office for a cybersecurity review before any public offering at a foreign stock exchange. PRC governmental authorities may also initiate cybersecurity review if they determine certain network products, services, or data processing activities affect or may affect national security. As of the date of this annual report, we are not aware of official release of detailed rules or implementation rules by any authority and we have not been informed that we are a critical information infrastructure operator by any government authorities. Furthermore, the scope of “network products or services or data processing activities that will or may affect national security” and the scope of operators of “critical information infrastructure” remains unclear, and the PRC government authorities may have wide discretion in the interpretation and enforcement of the applicable laws. ​ In the past, the PRC government has initiated cybersecurity reviews against a number of mobile applications operated by several US-listed Chinese companies and prohibited applications from registering new users during the review period. We expect that cybersecurity and data protection issues will receive greater and continued attention and scrutiny from regulators and the public going forward, which could increase our compliance costs and subject us to heightened risks and challenges associated with data security and protection, as well as negative publicity. If the Cybersecurity Review Measures mandates clearance of cybersecurity review and other specific actions to be taken by overseas listed companies like us, we face uncertainties as to whether we can complete these additional procedures timely, or at all, which may subject us to government enforcement actions and investigations, fines, penalties, revocation of the required licenses, suspension of our non-compliant operations, or removal of our mobile application from the application stores, and materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations. As of the date of this annual report, we have not been involved in any formal investigations on cybersecurity review made by the CAC on such basis. In September 2024, the State Council promulgated the Regulation on Network Data Security Management, which took effect January 1, 2025. This regulation restates and further specifies the additional legal requirements for personal information, important data, cross-border data transfer, network platform services, and data security. Among others, this regulation requires that if the network data processing activities affects or may affect national security, such activities shall be subject to national security review in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. However, there have been no clarifications from the authorities as of the date of this annual report as to the standards for determining whether an activity is one that “affects or may affect national security.” 27 Table of Contents In October 2025, the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress of China promulgated the revised PRC Cybersecurity Law, which took effect on January 1, 2026. This revised Cybersecurity Law further strengthens cybersecurity obligations, expands regulatory coverage, introduces requirements for artificial intelligence security, and significantly increases penalties for violations compared with the original version. However, as of the date of this annual report, no detailed implementation standards or clarification have been issued by the competent authorities with respect to the new and revised provisions under the updated Cybersecurity Law. In February 2026, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, together with the CAC, the NDRC, the National Data Administration, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Natural Resources, the Ministry of Transport, and the State Administration for Market Regulation formally issued the Guidelines for the Security of Cross-border Transfer of Automotive Data (2026 Edition), providing compliance guidance for cross-border data transfer activities as well as identification of important data in the automotive industry. As there are uncertainties with respect to the interpretation of certain provisions, we may be required to make further adjustments to our business practices to comply with the guidance. Personal Information and Privacy On August 16, 2021, the CAC, the NDRC, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology and the Ministry of Transport jointly promulgated the Several Provisions on Automobile Data Security Management (Trial Implementation), which impose a series of additional personal information and data security protection obligations on automobile data processors like us, including, among other things, (i) in-car processing of automobile data in principle, (ii) enhanced notification and consent requirements, (iii) enhanced individual control over their automobile personal information, and (iv) submitting annual report for processing automobile important data. We may be required to make further adjustments to our business practices to comply with the personal information and data protection laws and regulations. Many of the data-related legislations are relatively new and certain concepts thereunder remain subject to interpretation by the regulators. Moreover, different PRC regulatory bodies have enforced data privacy and protections laws and regulations with varying standards and applications. In general, compliance with the existing PRC laws and regulations, as well as additional laws and regulations that PRC regulatory bodies may enact in the future, related to data security and personal information protection, may be costly and result in additional expenses to us, and subject us to negative publicity, which could harm our reputation and business operations. There are also uncertainties with respect to how such laws and regulations will be implemented and interpreted in practice. In addition to the aforementioned PRC regulations, regulatory authorities in the U.S., Europe and elsewhere around the world have adopted or are considering a number of legislative and regulatory proposals concerning data protection. These legislative and regulatory proposals, if adopted, and the uncertain interpretations and application thereof could, in addition to the possibility of fines, result in an order requiring that we change our data practices and policies, which could have an adverse effect on our business and results of operations. For example, the European Union adopted the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) which took effect on May 25, 2018. This regulation includes operational requirements for companies that receive or process personal data of residents of the European Economic Area, and establishes new requirements applicable to the processing of personal data, affords new data protection rights to individuals and imposes penalties for serious data breaches. Individuals also have a right to compensation under this regulation for financial or non-financial losses. As we offer our products and services in European market, we are subject to provisions of this regulation. Although the GDPR has been in effect for years, data protection authorities and courts within the European Union member states have adopted varying interpretations of the GDPR.
